characterization_methods.key_findings: Austenite (FCC) and ferrite (BCC) peaks observed; BCC/ferrite fraction of 17.8 % for DP1000-5-TD (0.5 weight fraction column shares DP1000-5).
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase constituents and the ferrite fraction

characterization_methods.key_findings: Intragranular κ-carbide nanoparticles in DP1000-5 with size r = 0.86 ± 0.20 nm and f = 1.56 %; ferrite and austenite+κ-carbides indexed by SAED.
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify κ-carbide nanoparticles and Cr7C3 carbides and confirm ferrite/austenite phases
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with SAED and EDS

characterization_methods.key_findings: DP1000-5 (shared microstructure with DP1000-5-TD): Rex-γ 95.2 %, α 4.1 %, δ 9.3 %, uniform yellow GROD with black ferrite bands.
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase (PH) mappings and grain-reference-orientation-deviation (GROD) mappings of austenite; quantify constituent fractions and recrystallization

characterization_methods.key_findings: In DP1000-5-TD, cracks nucleate and propagate along RD-oriented δ ferrite bands whose δ/γ interfaces are perpendicular to the tensile axis.
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine microstructures and typical tensile cracks (crack nucleation, deflection, propagation)

characterization_methods.key_findings: In DP1000-5, ferrite is clearly softer than the recrystallized austenite.
characterization_methods.purpose: Study the mechanical response of different microstructural constituents

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Measured ferrite fractions (XRD) included for comparison: calculated ferrite fraction remains almost constant ~33 % between 991 and 1250 °C then increases to a maximum as temperature decreases from 991 to 854 °C, whereas the largest measured ferrite fraction appears at 900 °C.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: In DP1000-5-TD the δ/γ interfaces are perpendicular to the tensile direction and subjected to high de-cohesive stress; consequently, cracks were initiated at these δ/γ interfaces in addition to the α/γ interfaces, and then propagated until they quickly got connected across the full thickness during straining, leading to poor ductility (TE 18.1 % vs 41.4 % for DP1000-5).

defect_interactions.interaction_type: crack deflection/blunting by δ ferrite bands
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: In the RD-oriented case (DP1000-5) ND-propagating cracks are captured and deflected by δ ferrite bands parallel to RD and get blunted through dislocation emission and local plastic dissipation near the crack tip; the orientation of δ ferrite bands relative to the tensile axis is why TD loading gives lower ductility.

interfaces.interface_notes: The δ ferrite bands are the only microstructural constituent with a clear orientation, making them the most likely reason for the lower ductility measured along TD.
interfaces.phase_evolution: During annealing at 1000 °C, Cr7C3 carbides, intergranular κ-carbides and ferrite transform significantly to austenite, resulting in high Mn/Al/C concentrations in austenite for high-density nanosized κ-carbide precipitation during water quenching.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: DP1000-5-TD has similar YS/UTS but lower TE compared to DP1000-5 (18.1 % vs 41.4 %); attributed to δ ferrite bands whose δ/γ interfaces are perpendicular to the TD tensile axis

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Melted in a vacuum induction furnace under argon atmosphere.
Homogenization at 1200 °C for 2 h before hot rolling.
HR plates heated to 1050 °C and isothermally held for 0.5 h, then quenched in water.
Terminal annealing of DP1000-5-TD: annealed at 1000 °C for 5 min then quenched in water; identical treatment to DP1000-5 (specimen machined with length along TD).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Three tensile measurements were made for the heat treatment condition and the average values taken.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: flat dog-bone-shaped tensile specimen, gage length 25 mm, length direction along the transverse direction (TD)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve for DP1000-5-TD (dotted red) shown in Fig. 3a; dotted curve lies among the long curves (>40 % strain for DP1000-5/DP1050-1 group) but gives lower TE.

structures.microstructure_counts: Rex-γ fraction 95.2 %; α ferrite (EBSD) 4.1 %; δ ferrite (EBSD) 9.3 %; total ferrite (XRD) 17.8 %

phases_present.morphology: nearly fully recrystallized matrix with annealing twins

precipitates.distribution: within austenite grains (intragranular); volume fraction f = 1.56 %

phases_present.morphology: granular, located at austenite grain boundaries and triple points
band-like, elongated along the rolling direction (RD); sparse thin bands in DP1000-5

structures.overall_structure: Austenite-ferrite duplex microstructure produced by annealing the cold-rolled structure at 1000 °C for 5 min then water quenching: a nearly fully recrystallized austenitic matrix containing two types of ferrite — granular α ferrite grains and banded δ ferrite — together with intragranular nanoscale κ-carbide precipitates formed during water quenching. Microstructure is identical to DP1000-5 (same heat treatment); only the tensile specimen orientation differs (TD).

unmapped_findings: Specific yield strength (SYS) of DP1000-5-TD = 158.0 ± 2.4 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³ and specific ultimate tensile strength (SUTS) = 187.1 ± 2.4 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³ (Table 1, b0019).
DP1000-5-TD has similar YS/UTS but lower TE (18.1 ± 0.4 %) compared to DP1000-5 (TE 41.4 ± 0.5 %), attributed to the δ ferrite bands being the only clearly oriented constituent (b0027).

DP1000-5-TD is plotted as a red star (dotted-red engineering stress-strain curve) in Fig. 3b SUTS vs TE comparison; its SUTS×TE product does not exceed 8 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·% unlike DP1000-5 and DP1050-1 (figure_003).

DP1000-5-TD shares the identical terminal annealing microstructure with DP1000-5 (Rex-γ 95.2 %, γ grain size 7.40 ± 5.13 μm, ferrite fraction by XRD 17.8 %, α 4.1 %, δ 9.3 %); it is retained as a separate sample only to distinguish the TD-oriented tensile specimen (process entity note).
